claim: The life cycle of microorganisms is associated with dynamic metabolic transitions and complex cellular responses.
source: The life cycle of microorganisms is associated with dynamic metabolic transitions and complex cellular responses.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that sets up the context of the study.

claim: How metabolic signals control the progressive choreography of structural reorganizations observed in quiescent cells during a natural life cycle remains unclear.
source: In yeast, how metabolic signals control the progressive choreography of structural reorganizations observed in quiescent cells during a natural life cycle remains unclear.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: An integrated microfluidic device enables continuous single-cell tracking in a batch culture experiencing unperturbed nutrient exhaustion.
source: We have developed an integrated microfluidic device to address this question, enabling continuous single-cell tracking in a batch culture experiencing unperturbed nutrient exhaustion to unravel the coordination between metabolic and structural transitions within cells.
evidence: The abstract describes the development and capability of the experimental technique.

claim: A fraction of cells is unable to transition to respiratory metabolism and undergoes a reversible entry into a quiescence-like state leading to premature cell death.
source: Our technique reveals an abrupt fate divergence in the population, whereby a fraction of cells is unable to transition to respiratory metabolism and undergoes a reversible entry into a quiescence-like state leading to premature cell death.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Nonmonotonous internal pH fluctuations in respiration-competent cells orchestrate the successive waves of protein superassemblies formation that accompany the entry into a bona fide quiescent state.
source: Further observations reveal that nonmonotonous internal pH fluctuations in respiration-competent cells orchestrate the successive waves of protein superassemblies formation that accompany the entry into a bona fide quiescent state.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: An abrupt cytosolic glass transition occurs stochastically long after proliferation cessation.
source: This ultimately leads to an abrupt cytosolic glass transition that occurs stochastically long after proliferation cessation.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations in the results section.

claim: Budding yeast may undergo several metabolic transitions from fermentation to respiration, followed by entry into quiescence during its natural life cycle.
source: During its natural life cycle, budding yeast may undergo several metabolic transitions from fermentation to respiration, followed by entry into a reversible state of proliferation arrest known as quiescence (De Virgilio, 2012; Gray et al., 2004; Sun and Gresham, 2021; Miles et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Quiescence is an essential part of the microorganism life cycle that ensures cell survival over prolonged periods.
source: Despite quiescence being an essential part of the microorganism life cycle that ensures cell survival over prolonged periods (Fontana et al., 2010), it has received little attention compared to the analysis of biological processes in proliferative contexts.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fontana et al., 2010.

claim: Quiescent cells strongly differ from proliferating cells in terms of metabolic activity and gene expression.
source: Quiescent cells strongly differ from proliferating cells in terms of metabolic activity and gene expression (Gray et al., 2004; Miles et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Quiescent cells display structural rearrangements in the cytoskeleton, mitochondria, nuclear organization, and the appearance of protein superassemblies, clusters, and aggregates.
source: They also display a large body of structural rearrangements in the cytoskeleton, mitochondria, nuclear organization, and the appearance of protein superassemblies, clusters, and aggregates (Sagot and Laporte, 2019; Sun and Gresham, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The detailed sequence of events describing how the dynamics of metabolic cues during the natural life cycle drive the entry into quiescence is still missing.
source: In particular, the detailed sequence of events describing how the dynamics of metabolic cues during the natural life cycle drive the entry into quiescence is still missing.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Phenotypic variability exists in microbial ecosystems in the stationary phase.
source: Also, an essential feature of microbial ecosystems in the stationary phase (SP) is the existence of phenotypic variability (Campbell et al., 2016; Avery, 2006; Holland et al., 2014; Labhsetwar et al., 2013; Ackermann, 2015; Bagamery et al., 2020; Solopova et al., 2014) and history-dependent behaviors that lead to fate divergences (Balaban et al., 2004; Cerulus et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The coexistence of heterogeneous cell populations has been previously reported in quiescence.
source: In quiescence, the coexistence of heterogeneous cell populations has been previously reported (Allen et al., 2006; Laporte et al., 2018a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: How phenotypic diversity emerges in a clonal population during a natural life cycle remains elusive.
source: Nevertheless, how phenotypic diversity emerges in a clonal population during a natural life cycle remains elusive (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap and references a figure illustrating the question.

claim: Bridging the gap in understanding phenotypic diversity requires performing longitudinal tracking of individual cells over time in population-scale growth experiments.
source: Bridging this gap requires performing longitudinal tracking of individual cells over time. However, an important technical obstacle is that it must be done in population-scale growth experiments to allow cell proliferation to have a collective impact on the environment.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what is needed to address the research question.

claim: Previous work has used an abrupt transition to glucose starvation to study how cells reorganize upon entry into the stationary phase.
source: Previous work has used an abrupt transition to glucose starvation to study how cells reorganize upon entry into the SP in various biological contexts (Munder et al., 2016; Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Results from abrupt starvation experiments cannot be transposed to the context of entering quiescence during an undisturbed life cycle.
source: While this experimental framework may be helpful for studying standard properties of cells undergoing proliferation arrest, the results cannot be transposed to the context of entering quiescence during an undisturbed life cycle, in which cells undergo a sequence of metabolic transitions and feedback continuously into the composition of their environment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences between experimental conditions.

claim: Cells must experience a respiration phase to accumulate carbohydrates and reach a bona fide quiescence state.
source: Indeed, an essential condition to reach a bona fide quiescence state (i.e., the ability to recover proliferation after prolonged arrest) is that cells must experience a respiration phase (RP) to accumulate carbohydrates, which does not occur upon abrupt glucose starvation (Ocampo et al., 2012; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Different nutrient limitations lead to distinct quiescent states.
source: In addition, different nutrient limitations lead to distinct quiescent states (Klosinska et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The microfluidic platform allows continuous tracking of individual cells' fate during an unperturbed full life cycle for up to 10 days.
source: Here, we report the development of a microfluidic platform for single-cell ecology, allowing continuous tracking of individual cells' fate during an unperturbed full life cycle (up to 10 days).
evidence: This describes the capability of the developed experimental system.

claim: The diauxic shift witnesses a cell fate divergence, where a minority of cells experience a metabolic crash.
source: Using a fluorescent reporter of internal pH (Mouton et al., 2020; Miesenböck et al., 1998; Dechant et al., 2010; Munder et al., 2016), we observe that the diauxic shift (DS) witnesses a cell fate divergence, where a minority of cells experience a metabolic crash similar to that observed upon an abrupt starvation (Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using a pH reporter.

claim: Cells that experience a metabolic crash undergo a premature yet reversible induction of cellular reorganizations that coincide with limited survival.
source: Interestingly, our long-term tracking capabilities further reveal that these cells experience a premature yet reversible induction of cellular reorganizations that coincide with limited survival.
evidence: This finding is based on long-term tracking data from the study.

claim: Respiration-competent cells experience fluctuations in internal pH in sync with metabolic transitions.
source: In contrast, respiration-competent cells experience fluctuations in internal pH in sync with metabolic transitions that drive successive waves of cellular reorganizations and a stochastic switch to a glass transition of the cytoplasm long after proliferation cessation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on pH measurements and cellular observations.

claim: The device is composed of a 25 ml liquid yeast culture connected to a microfluidic device for single-cell observation.
source: To track individual cell behavior during an unperturbed life cycle, we set up a device composed of a 25 ml liquid yeast culture (YPD medium) connected to a microfluidic device for single-cell observation (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C, 1F).
evidence: This describes the experimental setup and references figures showing the device.

claim: A closed recirculation loop allows individual cells trapped in the microfluidic device to be imaged over time while experiencing the same environmental changes as the population liquid culture.
source: Thanks to a closed recirculation loop, individual cells trapped in the microfluidic device could be imaged over time while experiencing the same environmental changes as the population liquid culture.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the experimental design.

claim: A filtration device based on inertial differential migration was designed to prevent clogging in the microfluidic device due to high cell density.
source: To prevent clogging in the microfluidic device due to the high cell density in the culture (up to 109 cells/ml), we designed a filtration device based on inertial differential migration (Kuntaegowdanahalli and Papautsky, 2008).
evidence: This describes a technical solution implemented in the experimental design, with citation to the underlying principle.

claim: The filtration device has an efficiency superior to 99%, reducing the concentration of cells entering the device by two orders of magnitude.
source: Optical density (OD) and fluorescence measurements revealed a filtration efficiency superior to 99%, reducing the concentration of cells entering the device by two orders of magnitude (Figure 1—figure supplement 1– S1E), and allowing us to image the cells over up to 10 days.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of the filtration device performance.

claim: The same filtration device could sort S. pombe cells with 92% efficiency.
source: We also checked that the same filtration device could sort S. pombe cells with 92% efficiency, thus highlighting the versatility of the methodology.
evidence: This is an experimental validation of the device's versatility.

claim: The experimental setup successfully recapitulated the successive proliferation phases occurring at the population level upon carbon source exhaustion with single-cell resolution.
source: Using this methodology, we successfully recapitulated the successive proliferation phases occurring at the population level upon carbon source exhaustion with single-cell resolution (Richards, 1928), namely: a rapid exponential growth (doubling time = 84 ± 12 min) corresponding to glucose fermentation (referred to as the fermentation phase or FP in the following, from t = 0 to t = 5.5 hr), followed by a sharp growth arrest, or DS (from t = 5.5 to t = 13.9 hr); then, the resumption of a slow proliferative regime (doubling time = 307 ± 52 min) which is associated with the use of ethanol as a carbon source for a respiratory metabolism (RP, from t = 13.9 to t = 31.6 hr) and a final cell proliferation cessation occurring upon carbon source exhaustion, leading to SP, see Figure 1B, C and Figure 1—video 1.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation of the system with quantitative measurements and references to figures.

claim: The growth pattern observed is not specific to the BY strain used for the experiment.
source: To make sure that this growth pattern was not specific to the BY strain used for this experiment, we also made population growth measurements in various prototrophic and auxotrophic strains, and obtained similar results (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a control experiment validating the generality of the findings.

claim: Up to ~80% of cells reentered the cell cycle within 5 hr after refeeding with fresh YPD medium after 10 days.
source: By refeeding the cells with fresh YPD medium after 10 days, we observed that up to ~80 % of them reentered the cell cycle within 5 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 -S1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experiment.

claim: The reversibility of cell proliferation arrest confirms that cells establish bona fide quiescence in the growth conditions used.
source: This result confirmed the reversibility of cell proliferation arrest and testified that cells establish bona fide quiescence in our growth conditions (Laporte et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the refeeding experiment, supported by citation.

claim: A drop in medium pH has long been reported to coincide with the resources' exhaustion during microbial growth.
source: A drop in medium pH has long been reported to coincide with the resources' exhaustion during microbial growth (Burtner et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: How internal pH evolves over an entire life cycle has never been investigated.
source: Yet, how internal pH evolves over an entire life cycle has never been investigated.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: The ratiometric fluorescent probe pHluorin was used to measure cytosolic pH.
source: To address this, we used the ratiometric fluorescent probe of cytosolic pH, pHluorin (Figure 1D, Miesenböck et al., 1998; Mouton et al., 2020), which was calibrated to display the actual internal pH (Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1– S1I).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, with citations and reference to calibration data.

claim: The initial pH was around 7.7 and started to decline synchronously in all cells during the fermentation phase.
source: Using this readout, we observed that the pH, which was initially around 7.7, started to decline synchronously in all cells during the F phase (Figure 1E, F and Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from pH measurements.

claim: At the onset of the diauxic shift, most cells (88%, N = 466) abruptly reached a pH plateau around 6.9.
source: At the onset of the DS, most cells (88%, N = 466) abruptly reached a plateau (pH ~6.9, blue lines on Figure 1F) followed by a slight pH increase (up to pH ~7.2) that coincided with entry into a respiratory metabolism.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the pH data with sample size.

claim: A minority (12%, N = 466) of cells experienced a further drop in pH down to about 5.8 during the diauxic shift.
source: In contrast, a minority (12%, N = 466) of cells (Figure 1E and red lines on Figure 1F) experienced a further drop in pH down to about 5.8 during the DS.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the pH data with sample size.

claim: In the subpopulation with early pH drop, the fluorescence signal progressively disappeared, precluding reliable pH monitoring for more than 20 hr.
source: In this subpopulation, the fluorescence signal progressively disappeared, precluding monitoring the internal pH for more than 20 hr in a reliable manner.
evidence: This describes a technical limitation in measuring pH in certain cells.

claim: In cells with high internal pH during the diauxic shift, the pH gradually declined after reaching a local maximum during the respiration phase.
source: In cells with high internal pH during the DS, the pH gradually declined after reaching a local maximum during the R phase.
evidence: This describes the pH dynamics observed in respiration-competent cells.

claim: Cells with high internal pH during the diauxic shift experienced a sharp pH drop down to about 5.8 at very heterogeneous times during the stationary phase.
source: These cells then experienced a sharp pH drop down to about 5.8, which occurred at very heterogeneous times during the SP, unlike the cells with an early pH drop.
evidence: This describes the temporal heterogeneity in pH dynamics in respiration-competent cells.

claim: pH variations appeared to be in sync with the sequence of proliferation phases, suggesting that internal pH is a crucial marker of the cells' metabolic status during their life cycle.
source: Altogether, these observations revealed unprecedented dynamics of internal pH during the yeast life cycle: pH variations appeared to be in sync with the sequence of proliferation phases, suggesting that internal pH is a crucial marker of the cells' metabolic status during their life cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pH dynamics data.

claim: Continuous pH measurements unraveled a divergence in cell fate at the diauxic shift, leading to the early emergence of heterogeneity within the population.
source: These continuous pH measurements also unraveled a divergence in cell fate at the DS, leading to the early emergence of heterogeneity within the population, in line with previous observations made upon abrupt starvation (Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the pH measurements, supported by citation to similar observations.

claim: This phenomenon of fate divergence was also observed in a W303 strain.
source: This phenomenon was also observed in a W303 strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a validation of the finding in a different strain background.

claim: The activation of respiration is a crucial metabolic response to survive glucose deprivation.
source: Recent studies have shown that the activation of respiration was a crucial metabolic response to survive glucose deprivation (Weber et al., 2020), enabling carbohydrate storage (Ocampo et al., 2012) and long-term viability (Laporte et al., 2018a).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: A respiration defect is naturally observed in about 10% of cells upon proliferation cessation following glucose exhaustion.
source: Interestingly, it was shown that a respiration defect was naturally observed in about 10 % of cells upon proliferation cessation following glucose exhaustion (Laporte et al., 2018a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Cells with a late pH drop resumed growth and roughly doubled their biomass during the respiration phase.
source: We found that cells with a late pH drop resumed growth and roughly doubled their biomass during the R phase (blue lines on Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1) in agreement with Figure 1C.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of cell growth.

claim: Cells that experienced an early pH drop did not recover during the respiration phase.
source: In contrast, cells that experienced an early pH drop (red lines on Figure 2A) did not recover during the R phase, suggesting that they could not transition to respiratory metabolism.
evidence: This is an observation from growth measurements with an inference about metabolic status.

claim: Cells with early pH drop did not resume growth when adding lactate to the medium.
source: Indeed, these cells did not resume growth when adding lactate (i.e., a nonfermentable carbon source) to the medium neither (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental test of respiratory capacity using a nonfermentable carbon source.

claim: Most cells with early pH drop were still viable after 3 days in stationary phase, even though their survival declined faster than adapting cells.
source: However, most of them were still viable after 3 days in SP, even though their survival declined faster than adapting cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a measurement of cell viability over time.

claim: The mitochondrial network architecture appeared similar (tubular) in all cells before the diauxic shift.
source: Whereas the mitochondrial network architecture appeared similar (i.e., tubular) in all cells before the DS, proliferating cells in the R phase displayed a fragmented mitochondria phenotype typical of respiring cells (blue cell, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation of mitochondrial morphology using the Ilv3-mCherry marker.

claim: Proliferating cells in the respiration phase displayed a fragmented mitochondria phenotype typical of respiring cells.
source: Whereas the mitochondrial network architecture appeared similar (i.e., tubular) in all cells before the DS, proliferating cells in the R phase displayed a fragmented mitochondria phenotype typical of respiring cells (blue cell, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation of mitochondrial morphology in respiring cells.

claim: Nonproliferating cells underwent a globularization of their mitochondrial network.
source: In contrast, nonproliferating cells underwent a globularization of their mitochondrial network (red cell, Figure 2C and Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is an observation of mitochondrial morphology in non-respiring cells.

claim: About ~10% of the cells could not transition to a respiratory metabolism at t = 12 hr post-diauxic shift.
source: Based on the clear distinction in the aggregation index between adapting and nonadapting cells, we measured that about ~10 % of the cells could not transition to a respiratory metabolism (at t = 12 hr post-DS, Figure 2D), in agreement with previous findings (Laporte et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of the fraction of non-respiring cells, consistent with prior research.

claim: The mitochondrial globularization in nonadapting cells was temporally closely associated with the diauxic shift, starting as early as 1h20 (p < 0.05) after its onset.
source: Importantly, this quantification revealed that the mitochondrial globularization in nonadapting cells was temporally closely associated with the DS since it started as early as 1h20 (p < 0.05) after its onset (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is a quantitative temporal measurement with statistical significance.

claim: Proliferating and nonproliferating cells experienced divergent cell fates at the diauxic shift based on their ability to switch to respiration.
source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that proliferating and nonproliferating cells experienced divergent cell fates at the DS based on their ability to switch to respiration; hence, they were referred to as respiration positive (R+) and negative (R−), respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Respiratory deficient cells (ρ− cells) are common in the BY background due to the genetic instability of mitochondrial DNA.
source: Also, these results suggest that the inability of R− cells to activate a respiratory metabolism was either triggered by this metabolic challenge or, alternatively, preexisted the DS, knowing that respiratory deficient cells (i.e., ρ− cells) are common in the BY background (yet less so in W303 strains) due to the genetic instability of mitochondrial DNA (Dimitrov et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research about strain characteristics.

claim: All R+ cells maintained a functional preCox4-mCherry import from fermentation to respiration.
source: Using these markers, we first checked that all R+ cells maintained a functional preCox4-mCherry import from fermentation to respiration (i.e., they were ρ+ cells, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation using mitochondrial import markers.

claim: Among the R− cells, only a minority (19%) had a dysfunctional mitochondrial import before the diauxic shift, indicating a preexisting respiratory deficiency.
source: Then, we observed that among the R− cells, only a minority (i.e., 19%) had a dysfunctional mitochondrial import before the DS, indicating that they had a preexisting respiratory deficiency (see ρ− cells in Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement distinguishing preexisting from induced respiratory defects.

claim: The vast majority of R− cells (81%) transitioned from ρ+ to ρ− during the diauxic shift.
source: In contrast, the vast majority of R− cells (81%) transitioned from ρ+ to ρ− during the DS.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement showing that most respiratory defects are induced.

claim: The respiration defect observed in R− cells occurred concomitantly with the environmental switch and was not due to a preexisting condition.
source: This result demonstrates that the respiration defect observed in R− cells occurred concomitantly with the environmental switch and was therefore not due to a preexisting condition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mitochondrial import data.

claim: The progeny quite faithfully inherited the respiration defect (inheritance index = 0.52).
source: Also, we showed that the progeny quite faithfully inherited it (inheritance index = 0.52, i.e., is smaller than 1, see Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Material and methods for details).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of phenotype inheritance.

claim: A fate divergence occurred early at the onset of the diauxic shift, where R+ cells quickly switched to a respiratory metabolism, while R− cells failed to do so.
source: Altogether, these observations supported a scenario in which a fate divergence occurred early at the onset of the DS, where R+ cells quickly switched to a respiratory metabolism, while R− cells failed to do so.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion integrating multiple experimental observations.

claim: Numerous cellular reorganizations occur during entry into quiescence.
source: As numerous cellular reorganizations occur during entry into quiescence (Sagot and Laporte, 2019), we sought to quantitatively determine how they are coordinated with metabolic transitions during the life cycle.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Metabolism controls internal cellular pH, which in turn can induce significant physicochemical changes in the proteome, such as protein aggregation and phase transition.
source: Indeed, the metabolism controls internal cellular pH, which in turn can induce significant physicochemical changes in the proteome, such as protein aggregation and phase transition (Munder et al., 2016; Dechant et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The cellular reorganizations were highly coordinated with the sequence of metabolic phases and the cellular proliferation status.
source: We found that the cellular reorganizations were highly coordinated with the sequence of metabolic phases and the cellular proliferation status (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1): in R+ cells, Dhh1-GFP and Gln1-GFP (Figure 3—video 1) foci appeared at the onset of the DS, then were partially dissolved during the R phase, and reappeared upon entry into SP.
evidence: This is a primary finding from monitoring multiple cellular markers over time.

claim: In R+ cells, Dhh1-GFP and Gln1-GFP foci appeared at the onset of the diauxic shift, then were partially dissolved during the respiration phase, and reappeared upon entry into stationary phase.
source: We found that the cellular reorganizations were highly coordinated with the sequence of metabolic phases and the cellular proliferation status (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1): in R+ cells, Dhh1-GFP and Gln1-GFP (Figure 3—video 1) foci appeared at the onset of the DS, then were partially dissolved during the R phase, and reappeared upon entry into SP.
evidence: This describes the temporal dynamics of specific protein foci in respiring cells.

claim: Actin bodies, PSGs, and other protein foci (Cdc28-GFP) showed up only at the end of the respiration phase in R+ cells.
source: Other hallmarks of proliferation cessation, such as actin bodies, PSGs, and other protein foci (Cdc28-GFP), showed up only at the end of the R phase.
evidence: This describes the temporal appearance of additional cellular structures in respiring cells.

claim: R− cells experienced a consistent formation of fluorescent foci for the markers monitored, yet they all appeared during the diauxic shift.
source: Importantly, we observed that R− cells also experienced a consistent formation of fluorescent foci for the markers that we monitored, yet, unlike R+ cells, they all appeared during the DS.
evidence: This describes the temporal dynamics of protein foci in non-respiring cells.

claim: All foci in R− cells ultimately disappeared, presumably as a consequence of the premature cell death observed in this subpopulation.
source: In addition, all these foci ultimately disappeared, presumably as a consequence of the premature cell death observed in this subpopulation.
evidence: This is an observation with a speculative interpretation about the cause.

claim: The formation of bodies overall coincided with variation in absolute pH level in both R+ and R− cells.
source: By overlapping the dynamics of fluorescence foci formation with that of internal pH (from Figure 1F), we noticed that the formation of bodies overall coincided with variation in absolute pH level in both R+ and R− cells, even though it appeared at different timescales.
evidence: This is an observation from correlating pH dynamics with foci formation.

claim: A pH decrease down to ~7 would trigger the formation of Gln1 and Dhh1 foci in both R+ and R− cells upon the diauxic shift.
source: This finding is compatible with the hypothesis that the drop in internal pH – which reflects a decrease in metabolic activity – actually drives successive waves of body formation and the appearance of quiescence hallmarks. Indeed, upon the DS, a pH decrease down to ~7 would trigger the formation of Gln1 and Dhh1 foci in both R+ and R− cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the correlation between pH and foci formation.

claim: In R+ cells, the rerise of the pH associated with proliferation resumption in the respiration phase would induce the disassembly of Gln1 and Dhh1 structures until the pH reaches 7 again.
source: In R+ cells, the rerise of the pH associated with proliferation resumption in the R phase would induce the disassembly of these structures until the pH reaches 7 again, after carbon source exhaustion in SP.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the mechanism of foci disassembly based on pH dynamics.

claim: In both R+ and R−, actin bodies, PSG, and Cdc28 foci would form only when the intracellular pH reaches 6.
source: In both R+ and R−, actin bodies, PSG, and Cdc28 foci would form only when the intracellular pH reaches 6.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about pH-dependent formation of specific cellular structures.

claim: Energy depletion induces a global modification of the cytoplasm to a glassy state.
source: To further check this hypothesis, since energy depletion was shown to induce a global modification of the cytoplasm to a glassy state (Munder et al., 2016), we sought to observe these transitions by monitoring the frame-to-frame displacement of Gln1-GFP foci over time (Figure 3B, Munder et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The mobility of Gln1-GFP foci decreased sharply in R− cells during the diauxic shift.
source: We found that the mobility of Gln1-GFP foci decreased sharply in R− cells during the DS (Figure 3—video 1) and much later in R+ cells, consistently with the differences observed regarding the times of pH drops in both populations (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an observation of foci mobility dynamics.

claim: The mobility of Gln1-GFP foci decreased much later in R+ cells compared to R− cells, consistently with the differences in times of pH drops.
source: We found that the mobility of Gln1-GFP foci decreased sharply in R− cells during the DS (Figure 3—video 1) and much later in R+ cells, consistently with the differences observed regarding the times of pH drops in both populations (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an observation correlating mobility loss with pH dynamics.

claim: The time of loss of lipid droplet mobility correlated very well with that of Gln1-GFP foci.
source: Similarly, the time of loss of LDs mobility correlated very well with that of Gln1-GFP foci (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative correlation between two mobility measurements.

claim: The time of loss of lipid droplet mobility and the dynamics of pH drop in single cells were tightly correlated in all cells.
source: By quantifying both the time of loss of LD mobility and the dynamics of pH drop in single cells, we observed that both events were tightly correlated in all cells, despite the large cell-to-cell heterogeneity in the time of pH drop in R+ cells (Figure 3D , Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—source data 2 and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative correlation analysis between pH and mobility.

claim: The mobility loss of the cytoplasm occurred at a similar pH ~6 in both R+ and R− cells.
source: Also, after synchronizing all single-cell trajectories from the time of loss of LD mobility, we showed that the mobility loss of the cytoplasm occurred at a similar pH ~6 in both R+ and R− cells (Figure 3E, Figure 3—source data 2 and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement showing pH at the time of mobility loss.

claim: The internal pH, which displays a very dynamic behavior during the yeast life cycle, induces waves of cellular structural remodeling that ultimately triggers a global transition of the cytoplasm to a gel-like state.
source: Therefore, these observations suggest that the internal pH, which displays a very dynamic behavior during the yeast life cycle, induces waves of cellular structural remodeling that ultimately triggers a global transition of the cytoplasm to a gel-like state.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the correlation between pH dynamics and cellular reorganizations.

claim: Upon nutrient exhaustion, cells undergo stereotypical pH-dependent structural reorganizations, no matter their respiratory status.
source: Altogether, it suggests that, upon nutrient exhaustion, cells undergo stereotypical pH-dependent structural reorganizations, no matter their respiratory status.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from observations in both R+ and R− cells.

claim: R− cells' inability to switch to respiration makes the pH-dependent transition precocious and explains the divergent cell fates in the population at the diauxic shift.
source: R− cells' inability to switch to respiration, which ultimately compromises the long-term viability in this subpopulation (Ocampo et al., 2012; Weber et al., 2020), makes this transition precocious, and explains the divergent cell fates in the population at the DS.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation integrating multiple observations, supported by citations.

claim: The new microfluidic platform allows monitoring of a full cell proliferation cycle in liquid culture with single-cell resolution.
source: In this study, we have developed a new microfluidic platform that allows us to monitor a full cell proliferation cycle in liquid culture with single-cell resolution.
evidence: This summarizes the technical achievement of the study.

claim: Individual cell tracking and quantitative fluorescence measurements provide a unique dynamic assessment of the successive metabolic transitions from fermentation to the stationary phase.
source: Individual cell tracking and quantitative fluorescence measurements provide a unique dynamic assessment of the successive metabolic transitions from fermentation to the SP observed in a liquid culture submitted to nutrients exhaustion.
evidence: This describes the capability and application of the methodology.

claim: The methodology recapitulates the unperturbed dynamics of nutrients experienced by cells during a life cycle in laboratory conditions.
source: In contrast to most previous studies that used abrupt environmental switches to investigate the metabolic response to starvation, our methodology recapitulates the unperturbed dynamics of nutrients experienced by cells during a life cycle in laboratory conditions.
evidence: This highlights a key advantage of the methodology compared to prior approaches.

claim: The methodology could be further applied to other contexts in which collective cell behavior impacts the environment, which in turn shapes individual cellular responses.
source: We envision that this methodology could be further applied to other contexts in which collective cell behavior impacts the environment, which in turn shapes individual cellular responses – for example, metabolic oscillations (Tu et al., 2005) and cooperative behaviors (Dal Co et al., 2020; Campbell et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the methodology, with citations to relevant contexts.

claim: Continuous monitoring of cell growth and mitochondrial markers revealed a clear divergence in cell fate, where a minority failed to establish a respiratory metabolism.
source: Continuous monitoring of cell growth and mitochondrial markers revealed a clear divergence in cell fate, where a minority of them failed to establish a respiratory metabolism, in line with recent observations obtained using an abrupt medium change (Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This summarizes a key finding and relates it to prior work.

claim: The dramatic drop in internal pH upon proliferation cessation in R− cells at the diauxic shift suggests that the failure to transition to respiration induces a major loss of energy homeostasis.
source: The dramatic drop in internal pH upon proliferation cessation in R− cells at the DS suggests that the failure to transition to respiration induces a major loss of energy homeostasis in this subpopulation, that may, in turn, compromise long-term viability (Ocampo et al., 2012; Weber et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pH data with citations supporting the connection to viability.

claim: The phenomenon of fate divergence could not be explained by preexisting phenotypic differences in the population during the fermentation phase but rather appeared to be triggered by the metabolic challenge associated with the exhaustion of glucose.
source: By and large, this phenomenon could not be explained by preexisting phenotypic differences in the population during the FP (Bagamery et al., 2020) but rather appeared to be triggered by the metabolic challenge associated with the exhaustion of glucose.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the origin of fate divergence, with citation to related work.

claim: Changes in cytosolic pH control protein supramolecular assemblies.
source: Previous studies have unraveled how changes in cytosolic pH – including upon nutrient exhaustion – control protein supramolecular assemblies (Peters et al., 2013; Petrovska et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Nonmonotonous fluctuations in pH level occur in sync with metabolic transitions during an unperturbed life cycle.
source: Our analysis shows that nonmonotonous fluctuations in pH level occur in sync with metabolic transitions during an unperturbed life cycle.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the pH measurements.

claim: Successive pH drops are closely temporally related to the formation of many protein bodies and granules, despite large cell-to-cell temporal variability.
source: Further, it reveals that successive pH drops are closely temporally related to the formation of many protein bodies and granules, despite the large cell-to-cell temporal variability associated with the onset of these events.
evidence: This describes the temporal correlation between pH and cellular structures.

claim: Internal pH acts as a key controller that drives waves of structural changes at well-defined pH levels during entry into quiescence.
source: Interestingly, since the structural reorganization of many protein complexes is one of the well-described hallmarks of quiescence (Sagot and Laporte, 2019), our observations thus suggest that internal pH acts as a key controller that drives waves of structural changes at well-defined pH levels during entry into quiescence.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed based on the data, with citation to prior knowledge about quiescence.

claim: R− cells display foci formation similarly as the R+ cells, providing further support to a model of stereotypical structural reorganizations driven by energy depletion and transduced by internal pH level.
source: That R– cells display foci formation similarly as the R+ cells provide further support to a model of stereotypical structural reorganizations driven by energy depletion and transduced by internal pH level.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similarity in foci formation between cell types.

claim: The transition to stationary phase is accompanied by a transition of the cytoplasm to a glassy-like phase.
source: In addition to monitoring the superassembly of specific markers, we showed that the transition to SP is accompanied by a transition of the cytoplasm to a glassy-like phase, hence transposing previous observations (Parry et al., 2014; Joyner et al., 2016; Munder et al., 2016) to the context of an unperturbed life cycle in budding yeast (Heimlicher et al., 2019).
evidence: This finding extends prior observations to the context of an unperturbed life cycle, with citations.

claim: The appearance of the glassy-like state occurs right at the diauxic shift in R− cells and is significantly delayed and variable in time in R+ cells.
source: Importantly, the appearance of the glassy-like state occurs right at the DS in the R– cells and is significantly delayed and variable in time in R+ cells.
evidence: This describes the temporal differences in glass transition between cell types.

claim: The start of respiration upon glucose exhaustion prevents a precocious glass transition, which might be detrimental to cell viability if it occurs in an uncoordinated manner with other cellular reorganizations processes.
source: We propose that the start of respiration upon glucose exhaustion prevents a precocious glass transition, which might be detrimental to cell viability if it occurs in an uncoordinated manner with other cellular reorganizations processes (e.g., energy storage)(Ocampo et al., 2012; Weber et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a proposed model with speculative elements about the consequences, supported by citations.

claim: The abrupt and concomitant transition of all cells during the diauxic shift shows how the rapid evolution of the environment drives cell behavior in a deterministic manner.
source: The abrupt and concomitant transition of all cells during the DS shows how the rapid evolution of the environment at this precise moment drives cell behavior in a deterministic manner, in the same way as during abrupt starvation (Bagamery et al., 2020; Munder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the synchronous response at the diauxic shift, with citations to similar observations.

claim: The remarkable cell-to-cell temporal heterogeneity during the transition to a glassy state in R+ cells suggests that the cells have a developmental program whose progression is partly stochastic.
source: Conversely, the remarkable cell-to-cell temporal heterogeneity during the transition to a glassy state in R+ cells suggests that the cells have a developmental program whose progression is partly stochastic, that is, not entirely determined by the external environment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the heterogeneity observed in R+ cells.

claim: It is impossible to follow the process of entry into quiescence faithfully by imposing the dynamics of environmental changes or based on population measurements only.
source: This last observation further supports that it is impossible to follow the process of entry into quiescence faithfully by imposing the dynamics of environmental changes (Miles et al., 2021) or based on population measurements only.
evidence: This is a conclusion about methodological requirements, with citation.

claim: The filtration device was designed with a spiral-shaped microfluidic channel of 100 µm width and 50 µm height, defining a spiral of five loops separated by 900 µm.
source: The dimensions of the cell filter (i.e., a channel of 100 µm width and 50 µm height, defining a spiral of five loops separated by 900 µm) were set to maximize the separation of haploid yeast cells, that is, ~5 μm particles, according to the following principle: particles in a spiral microfluidic channel with a rectangular section are submitted to several inertial forces that depend on their size and are either directed towards the center of the channel or the walls.
evidence: This describes the technical specifications of the filtration device.

claim: Particles of similar diameters reach an equilibrium position and tend to focus on a single line in a spiral microfluidic channel, allowing their separation from the rest of the fluid.
source: Therefore, particles of similar diameters reach an equilibrium position and tend to focus on a single line, allowing their separation from the rest of the fluid by splitting the output channel in two different outlets.
evidence: This explains the physical principle underlying the filtration device.

claim: A similar filter could be used with other microorganisms by adapting the dimensions.
source: A similar filter could be used with other microorganisms by adapting the dimensions.
evidence: This is a speculation about the adaptability of the technology.

claim: The filtration efficiency was equal to 99% in both turbidity and fluorescence measurements, independently of the inlet cell concentration.
source: The filtration efficiency was equal to 99 % in both measurements, independently of the inlet cell concentration.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of device performance.

claim: Cells were imaged using motorized stages to follow up to 64 positions in parallel throughout the experiment.
source: We used motorized stages to follow up to 64 positions in parallel throughout the experiment.
evidence: This describes the imaging capability of the experimental setup.

claim: Single plane images were acquired every 15, 30, 60, or 240 min depending on the phase of the culture to limit photodamage.
source: Single plane images were acquired every 15 , 30 , 60 , or 240 min depending on the phase of the culture (high sampling rate during FP versus lower acquisition frequency in SP) to limit photodamage.
evidence: This describes the imaging protocol used in the experiments.
